date_and_recency: Data window 2026-07-30 to 2026-08-28 for the review figures. Page text says output snapshot as of 2026-06-09, which is earlier than the data window, so the page is internally inconsistent on dates. [uncertain] Publication date not stated.
key_claims: Most merged agent PRs in significant public repos carry no human GitHub reviewer (56%); the review rate varies widely by agent (Copilot and Cursor high, Jules low); high merge rate with low review rate means the agent self-merges. The page also reports median time to merge and share of PRs touching tests per agent, and a separate settled-window merge rate table.
headline_figures: Overall: 268 merged agent PRs, 44% human-reviewed, 56% merged with none (significant repos, 2026-07-30 to 2026-08-28). Human-reviewed share / median time to merge / touches tests: GitHub Copilot 80.5% / 33 min / 31.7%; Cursor 77.8% / 1.02h / 55.8%; Devin 51.6% / 23 min / 45.8%; ZCode 31.6% / 20 min / 60.8%; Claude Code 30.5% / 38 min / 47.5%; OpenAI Codex 28.6% / 8 min / 69.2%; Jules 12.5% / 57 min / 25%. Merge rates (settled window): ZCode 91.7%, Claude Code 91.6%, OpenAI Codex 87.3%, Kilo Code 78.7%, Cursor 71.1%, CodeRabbit 70.3%, Copilot 68.2%, Devin 68.1%, Jules 63.4%, Amazon Q Developer 62.3%, Factory Droid 45%, Vercel Agent 33.1%. NOTE: the brief quoted 230 PRs and 44.3% with no reviewer; the source says 268 and 44% WITH a reviewer, 56% with none. The brief's figures do not match the live page.
sample_unit_and_population: Unit is the merged agent pull request. 268 merged PRs across 'significant' public GitHub repos (org-owned or 10+ stars). Open-source/public only; no enterprise or private repos. Per-agent subsample sizes are not given on the .md page, so per-agent percentages rest on unknown and probably small n. [uncertain]
observed_vs_stated: Observed: public GitHub activity (reviewer fields, merge times, files touched). No self-report. Agent attribution is inferred from public signatures.
what_makes_trust_justified: The page does not argue for a trust mechanism. It frames a human non-author, non-bot reviewer as the signal of human sign-off and treats absence of one as self-merge. Test inclusion is reported as a secondary signal.
what_it_costs: Not quantified as a cost. Median time to merge is reported (8 min Codex to 1.02h Cursor), and the highest-review agents (Cursor, Copilot, Jules) are not uniformly slower, so review cost is confounded with agent and repo type.
failure_mode_class: Over-reliance / absent oversight (merging agent work with no independent human reviewer). No incidents of wrong code or harm are measured.
control_that_would_have_prevented: Not an incident study. Implied control is a required non-author human review before merge; the page does not measure whether that would have caught anything.
limitations_stated: "public repositories only; private-repo work is not counted. Squash-merges and disabled attribution further undercount." "Treat every figure as a floor and a proxy for the ecosystem, not a census." Declared-attribution counts "can swing 30 to 40 percent between runs". Visibility classes (Exact, Estimate, No public signature) are unequal.
counter_evidence: Not in source. Own reasoning: 'no GitHub reviewer' is not 'no review'. Solo maintainers, bot-only repos, direct pushes of personal projects, and review done offline or via comments (not formal review) all count as unreviewed. A repo with 10+ stars can be a single-person project, so the 56% may mostly reflect solo repos where an author merging their own PR is normal. The page itself says review rate is not the same as approval. No comparison group of human-authored PRs is given, so 56% has no baseline. [uncertain]
verification_status: Opened and read the primary .md page in full: figures, definition of reviewed, and limitations verified. Not verified: the methodology page (not read), per-agent sample sizes, how 'significant repos' were sampled, how agent attribution was done, the 2026-06-09 snapshot date versus the 2026-07/08 window. Brief's 230 and 44.3% not found on the page. [uncertain]
usable_claim: In one vendor index's sample of 268 merged agent PRs in public repos with 10+ stars or org ownership (30 July to 28 August 2026), 56% were merged with no non-author, non-bot GitHub reviewer, and the rate varied from about 20% reviewed (Jules 12.5%) to about 80% (Copilot 80.5%). The publisher itself calls the figures a floor and a proxy, not a census.
do_not_use: Do not use 230 or 44.3% (not on the page). Do not say 'no human looked at it' (it only means no formal non-author reviewer). Do not rank agents on trustworthiness from per-agent percentages (unknown n, estimated attribution). Do not generalise to private or enterprise repos. Do not call this peer-reviewed or an independent study.
overlap_with_existing_essays: Unknown. Not checked against The Verification Gap or Checking Isn't Catching essays in this task. [uncertain]
